claim.statement: The gamma band center frequency of 45 Hz is a load-bearing architectural constant in Kimera-SWM. It determines the Routh-Hurwitz amplitude-death threshold τ_crit = 1/(4·f_γ) = 5.56 ms, which is the literal mortality condition for 68.5% of cognitive acts. Changing f_γ would shift the lifetime of every reasoning act proportionally.
claim.operationalization: Identify the f_γ constant in cognitive_rhythm.py. Compute τ_crit = 1/(4·f_γ). Verify this is the threshold used in the M2 rule (line 683-686). Verify the M2 rule fires in 68.5% of cycles.
claim.h0: Gamma frequency is not load-bearing for the amplitude_death gate
claim.h1: Gamma frequency directly determines the amplitude_death threshold

preregistration.analysis_plan: Locate f_γ in code; verify it determines τ_crit; check rate of M2 firing.

detail.physics_basis: Routh-Hurwitz stability for time-delayed coupled oscillators

detail.interpretation: 68.5% of cycles end at this constant's threshold

verdict.reasoning: f_γ = 45 Hz literally documented in the comment at cognitive_rhythm.py:666 ('_TAU_CRIT_GAMMA_S = 1/(4*f_γ) = 1/(4*45) ≈ 5.56 ms'). This is the architectural constant determining cognitive-act mortality. Any change to f_γ would proportionally shift the lifetime of every act.
